portion_doctrine: High-level business interviews spanning African real estate market strategy, fashion brand scaling via founder CEO positioning, and Dubai water park entrepreneurship. Three distinct founder archetypes distilled: (1) real estate enabler focusing on diaspora education and formalized deal structures, (2) luxury lifestyle brand builder using scientific design thinking and celebrity validation, (3) bootstrap founder surviving bankruptcies to scale infrastructure. Common threads: founder resilience, speed of execution, leveraging information asymmetry, building systems before scaling locations, organic community growth, and running operations as lean businesses with clarity-first decision making.
operating_rules: Always use formal channels (notaries, real estate agents, escrow) never informal intermediaries
Perfect one unit before scaling to multiple locations (1 park, then 2, then scale)
Build written systems and documentation for every business step before hiring team
Listen to customer desires vs. imposing design; organic growth beats mileage chasing
Avoid ego investments (prestige projects without market due diligence)
Capped decision meetings at 20 minutes with clear points 1-3, problem statement, 3 solutions
Hire smart people, delegate authority plus equity, accept 60% execution while you free up elsewhere
Every interaction creates emotion; use storytelling and authentic documentation in social proof
Master one discipline deeply before pivoting to adjacent verticals
Government as business: compete on customer satisfaction, not bureaucracy
Run business as bootstrapped operation until proof; revenue > external investment
Treat bankruptcy as lesson not loss if you keep moving
Information access is the highest-leverage gap in emerging markets
Personal network + direct relationship building beats institutional sales early
